title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
evidence: Figure 3 and section 3: NLL can worsen while classification error improves.
limit: Classification evidence; our combined BCE+Dice loss needs decomposition.

title: Confidence Calibration and Predictive Uncertainty Estimation for Deep Medical Image Segmentation
evidence: Brain/heart/prostate segmentation; compares CE and Dice calibration; VI-A uses validation DSC checkpoint selection and plateau LR reduction.
limit: Different organs/models; ours uses combined BCE+Dice.

title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
evidence: LP-FT can mitigate feature distortion under studied classification distribution shifts.
limit: Does not establish catastrophic forgetting in MambaVision/ISIC; our fine-tuning outperforms frozen control.

title: Explicit Inductive Bias for Transfer Learning with Convolutional Networks
evidence: L2-SP regularizes weights towards pretrained initialization.
limit: Ordinary AdamW weight decay is not this regularizer; benefit here untested.

title: Budgeted Training: Rethinking Deep Neural Network Training Under Resource Constraints
evidence: Budget-aware LR schedules compared on classification, detection and segmentation; truncating a long schedule differs from a schedule matched to a short budget.
limit: Does not prove our encoder needs a particular decay horizon.

title: Improving Data-Efficiency and Robustness of Medical Imaging Segmentation Using Inpainting-Based Self-Supervised Learning
evidence: Appendix B compares transfer choices and LRs; immediate encoder fine-tuning at 1e-3 was preferred in their setup; too small LR also underperformed.
limit: Counterevidence to universally prescribing warmup or ever-smaller LR; absolute LR not portable.

title: How to build the best medical image segmentation algorithm using foundation models: a comprehensive empirical study with Segment Anything Model
evidence: 18 adaptation combinations on 17 medical datasets; parameter-efficient adaptation strong in their comparisons.
limit: SAM-specific study, not proof adapters outperform our MambaVision baseline.

title: Post hoc calibration of medical segmentation models
evidence: Calibration can improve without a matching Dice improvement; some methods/tasks lose Dice.
limit: Calibration diagnosis is not a guaranteed segmentation remedy.

title: Deep Networks with Stochastic Depth
evidence: Random residual branch dropping during training is a regularization/training technique.
limit: Original ResNet study; no guaranteed benefit for this small-data fine-tuning.

title: PyTorch Autograd mechanics: Evaluation Mode
evidence: eval is orthogonal to gradient disabling; training-mode-dependent modules change behavior.
limit: Current web docs checked against local Torch 2.2.2 and actual model.

title: timm DropPath implementation
limit: Local installed timm 1.0.22 source also checked; runtime_mode_audit.json confirms.

title: nnU-Net trainer defaults
evidence: Default 1000 epochs, 250 iterations/epoch; epoch counts cannot be compared across recipes directly.
limit: Not an argument to train our transfer model for 1000 epochs.
